candidateOutcomes: Lattice is a local-inference gateway: a hosted broker that routes Athena's model calls to models running on the user's own device. This follows WIL-41 ("models running on that device power Athena's work") and WIL-49, and ships as a model-provider adapter behind Docket's existing provider seam plus an OAuth connection managed in Settings.

Lattice is an agent platform whose skills Athena installs and invokes. This follows WIL-43 ("the appropriate Lattice skill is found, installed, and used to build the integration"), which reads oddly under the gateway reading, and ships as a capability/tool integration with a different surface, a different OAuth scope set (WIL-48), and a different offline failure mode.
questions.whyPlanCannotDecide: The plan names the product but never identifies the vendor, and every independent probe for its identity came back empty: a repo grep hits only the audit baseline, `grep -ci lattice pnpm-lock.yaml` returns 0, three DNS lookups return NXDOMAIN, and a live web search returns three unrelated products also called Lattice. WIL-42 requires building on the Lovelace Lattice SDK rather than a hand-rolled client and WIL-46 requires a turnkey connection with no hand-entered endpoints or keys, so both readings presuppose a specific named SDK and issuer that the plan text does not supply. The single input needed is the SDK package name or the OAuth issuer URL. Full probe output: docs/engineering/launch/external-systems.md § Lovelace Lattice; the entry is Q-01 in docs/engineering/launch/questions.md.

entries.evidence: docs/engineering/launch/launch-checklist.md enumerates all 399 audited ids with an owner, a state, and evidence for each, is regenerated from the audit and the slice files by scripts/launch-record.ts, regenerates byte-identically on a second run, and signOffViolations() withholds sign-off while any id is in a state other than closed. Two clauses of the acceptance are still open, so the entry is not closed: 385 of the 399 ids are not-started and therefore map to no landed commit or shipped deliverable, and nothing this lane produced is committed — git status --porcelain reports docs/engineering/launch/, the generator script, docs/design/surface-inventory.md, and the new policy suites untracked, because the run that produced them was instructed not to commit. Committing them is a single act; closing the other 385 ids is the launch itself.

The record policy test fails any blocked entry whose cause is documentation-unavailable, fetch-failed, paywalled-docs, or js-only-docs, and any blockedReason detail that phrases the same excuse in prose, so an unreachable doc site cannot be recorded as a stopping point.

The same blocked-entry policy rejects the causes missing-permission, missing-access, missing-credentials, and could-not-sign-in, so no open item in docs/engineering/launch/launch-record.json can state lack of access as its reason for stopping.

docs/engineering/launch/launch-record.json carries an externalSystems ledger for all seven systems GEN-05 names. Google, Notion, Cloudflare, and Vercel each record a captured authenticated call; Sunsama, Lovelace Lattice, and Twilio each record three or more distinct workaround attempts with their real failure output. signOffViolations() withholds sign-off until every system meets one of those two bars, and reports zero external-system violations today.

The bearer-token input is the only password-typed field across web and admin and renders as filled dots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in both themes; McpIntegrationOut carries no token field and apps/api/src/routes/integrations-mcp.ts seals the value with AES-256-GCM via sealCredential(). The verifier's probe-report.json records bearerFieldMasked true, leakingResponses empty, and zero of the captured responses containing the probe token, and a stored connector's expanded Connection details renders the server URL with no credential at all. The server-log clause of the acceptance rests on the sealCredential() path rather than a captured log sweep, which is recorded as a residual.

entries.evidence: The record carries a questions array in which every question must name the requirement id it blocked, two or more defensible outcomes, and why the plan text selects neither; questionViolations() fails any question missing one of the three and reports zero violations. One question is recorded — Q-01 against WIL-41, asking whether Lovelace Lattice is a local-inference gateway or an agent-skill platform — and it carries all three fields, so the measurable clause holds. The previous evidence here claimed the questions array was empty, which the same file contradicted.

verificationViolations() rejects a closed entry whose verifiedBy names the same agent as its owner under any casing, separator, or -verifier/-verification/-reviewer/-checker suffix, and rejects an entry citing only implementer-authored files: at least one artifact must be verifier-produced output under docs/engineering/launch/evidence/ or docs/design/audits/screenshots/. Both rules are proved against fixtures in both directions. The seven entries that had read owner launch-governance / verifiedBy launch-governance-verifier were re-verified by launch-record-reconciler, which wrote none of the slices it checked and captured its run to docs/engineering/launch/evidence/verification/2026-08-02-launch-record-reconciliation.txt — the artifact verification-log.md had recorded as the one thing missing.
